question: Will COP31 in Antalya close more than 24 hours after its scheduled end?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: 7 of the last 10 COPs (COP21-COP30) closed more than 24h after the scheduled Friday close, and 6 of the last 7. COP30 Belem closed Saturday 20:44. Pushing toward a late close: the presidency-led cover decision, fossil-fuel and mitigation work programme fights, adaptation-finance tripling disputes, just transition mechanism scope, trade measures, and the untested Turkey host / Australia negotiations-lead setup. Pushing toward an earlier close: no headline mandated deliverable, low expectations, Bowen's wish to avoid a lengthy negotiated statement, and the precedent of the implementation COPs (COP22, COP23), which ended early Saturday. Many recent closes fell on Saturday evening near the 18:00 threshold, so I stay modestly above the base rate rather than far above it. No human prediction market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- COP31 runs Mon Nov 9 to Fri Nov 20, 2026, at Antalya; Turkey hosts, and Australia's Chris Bowen is President of Negotiations (Climate Home and Geneva Environment Network, 2026).
- COP30 Belem closing plenary was gavelled at 20:44 local on Saturday Nov 22, 2025, one day after the scheduled Friday close (ENB summary; Carbon Brief).
- Historical closes, from memory except COP30: COP21 Paris Sat late evening; COP22 Marrakech early Sat; COP23 Bonn ~07:00 Sat; COP24 Katowice Sat late evening; COP25 Madrid Sun midday; COP26 Glasgow Sat evening; COP27 Sharm Sun morning; COP28 Dubai Wed midday (scheduled Tue, under 24h late); COP29 Baku Sun ~03:00; COP30 Belem Sat 20:44.
- Base rate, closed more than 24h after scheduled end: 7/10 for COP21-30; 6/7 for COP24-30. Implementation-type COPs with no major mandated deliverable (COP22, COP23) closed before the threshold. Several 'yes' cases closed on Saturday evening, within a few hours of 18:00.
- The Australia/Turkey presidency announced at the Oct 7, 2026 pre-COP that it will prepare a presidency-led cover decision. It does not want to negotiate a lengthy political statement (Climate Home, Oct 7, 2026).
- Planned cover decision contents: 1.5C overshoot, electrification target (35% by 2035), methane, early warning systems, adaptation finance access, nature (Climate Home briefing, Nov 5, 2026).
- Contested items: possible dissolution of the mitigation work programme and fossil-fuel transition language (LDCs/AOSIS vs Saudi Arabia/India/China); adaptation finance tripling baseline and delivery (African Group); just transition mechanism scope (Like-Minded Developing Countries); trade measures/EU carbon border levy (China); IPCC AR7 timeline (Climate Home, Nov 5, 2026).
- An EU official says no 'revolution' is expected; Bowen says consensus 'will not be easy' (Jakarta Post/AFP, Nov 8, 2026).
- Status quo for recent COPs: overtime into Saturday or later.
- Resolves off the IISD ENB COP31 summary closing time (fallback: UNFCCC webcast or credible media), and off the last of the COP/CMP/CMA closing plenaries, not the adoption of any single decision.
- Event window: closing plenary time vs. threshold Sat Nov 21 18:00 UTC+3; as of Nov 8 the conference has not yet started (0% of the Nov 9-21 window elapsed).
- Searched for Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold markets on COP31 timing: none found. Searched for an on-time pledge by the presidency: none found.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: COP17-COP30 closing times relative to scheduled end; ~11/14 closed >24h late (COP30 gavelled 20:44 Sat; COP29 Sunday early hours), but several were Saturday-evening near-misses and the on-time cases (COP22, COP23, COP28) were lower-stakes or tightly managed. COP31 has no mandated headline deliverable like NCQG and fossil roadmap is not a formal agenda item, which argues for quicker close; but adaptation-finance tripling baseline is unresolved, Australia seeks an ambitious cover decision, and the Türkiye/Australia split presidency adds friction risk. Net shade down from ~75% base rate to the mid-60s. No human prediction market found.
calls.dossier:
- Schedule: COP31 Antalya Expo Center, Nov 9-20 2026 (Fri); leaders' segment Nov 11-12. Turkey hosts and holds the COP31 presidency; Australia (Chris Bowen) is President of Negotiations (DCCEEW, Wikipedia).
- Threshold: YES only if the final COP/CMP/CMA closing plenary is gavelled after 18:00 Turkey time (UTC+3) on Sat Nov 21. A close on Saturday morning or afternoon resolves NO.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the IISD ENB COP31 summary closing time, falling back to UNFCCC webcast or credible media; it does not resolve off the scheduled dates.
- Event window: opening Nov 9 -> closing plenary; the cutoff is Nov 21 18:00 UTC+3. As of Nov 8 the conference has not started (0% elapsed).
- COP30 Belém (scheduled end Fri Nov 21 2025): final gavel 20:44 Sat Nov 22, after a turbulent closing plenary with points of order (ENB; Power Shift Africa).
- Historical closes (from memory, not checked this session): COP17 Sun; COP18 Sat evening; COP19 Sat evening; COP20 early Sun; COP21 ~19:30 Sat; COP22 early Sat (before cutoff); COP23 Sat morning (before cutoff); COP24 late Sat; COP25 Sun afternoon; COP26 Sat night; COP27 Sun morning; COP28 Wed ~midday, about 19h after its Tue end (before cutoff); COP29 early Sun. That is about 11/14 past the 24h mark, with several Saturday-evening near-misses. Rate over lower-stakes 'implementation' COPs (22, 23): 0/2. Over COPs with a big mandated deliverable: higher.
- Agenda (Climate Home briefing, Nov 5 2026): Australia aims for a cover decision (1.5C overshoot language, Turkish electrification pledge, methane, early warning, finance access, nature) and possibly the fossil fuel transition roadmap, which is contentious. Described as consequential: the first COP facing near-certain 1.5C overshoot. Leader attendance is lower.
- Contested items: tripling adaptation finance by 2035 (no agreed baseline or roadmap); NCQG follow-up. The fossil fuel phase-out is not a formal agenda item (IBA, other previews).
- Co-presidency friction risk: Türkiye says it has the 'final say' over Antalya (Climate Home).
- Markets: none found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi.
- Searched, not found: any presidency statement on ending on time; venue contract end-date constraints.

calls.reasoning: Base rate: Carbon Brief counts 8 of the 10 summits up to COP27 as running more than 24h late; adding COP28 (~23h, No), COP29 (~35h, Yes) and COP30 (~26.7h, closed 20:44 Sat, Yes) keeps a recent rate of roughly 70-80%. Adjustments down: COP31 is framed as an 'implementation COP' with no big mandated deliverable (comparable implementation COPs COP22/COP23 closed under 24h late), and recent overruns (COP28, COP30) sat close to the 24h line, so a near miss is quite possible. Adjustments up: finance (tripling adaptation finance) and the fossil-fuel/electrification cover-decision language are still disputed, plus the split Turkey/Australia arrangement. No human prediction market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold.

Presidency wants a cover decision with an electrification goal (20% to 35% of final energy by 2035); EU clean-electrification push may spark a fight over fossil-fuel language; African group seeks tripled adaptation finance; developed countries resisting.
- Structure: Türkiye hosts, Australia (Chris Bowen) presides over negotiations, an unprecedented split (DCCEEW, AA).
- Geopolitics and Middle East energy instability cited as complicating factors (AA / Türkiye Today).

calls.reasoning: Recent COPs closed >24h late roughly 70-80% of the time (7/10 COP21-30; Carbon Brief 8/10 to COP27). Shade down because COP31 is an implementation COP without a mandated headline deliverable (COP22/COP23 analogues closed early Saturday) and many recent overruns ended Saturday evening close to the 18:00 threshold. Partly offset by contested cover-decision content (fossil/electrification language, adaptation finance tripling baseline) and untested Türkiye/Australia split presidency. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same reference class and very similar evidence; disagreements are minor factual details of historical close times (all from memory except COP27-30 via Carbon Brief/ENB) and the judgment of how much to discount for the 'implementation COP' framing. Historical counts differ by ~1 case and don't move the anchor materially (~0.72-0.79). No web access to verify COP22/23 times; carried with uncertainty. Judgment: the low-stakes framing and near-threshold Saturday-evening clustering justify shading the base rate down to mid-60s; I agree with the runs and land at 0.64. No market found by any run or the harness.
